capability_declaration.evidence: ISO 15118-2:2014 Clause 8.3 (Service Discovery) and ISO 15118-20:2022 Clause 7.3 (EVCC-SECC capability exchange). The standard mandates that the EV Communication Controller (EVCC) and Supply Equipment Communication Controller (SECC) exchange supported services, protocols, and parameters — including charging modes (AC/DC), maximum power, scheduling capability, and V2G readiness — during session setup via the SupportedAppProtocolReq/Res handshake.
capability_declaration.rationale: ISO 15118 explicitly requires both vehicle and charger to declare their capabilities — charging power, scheduling support, V2G, metering — before any energy transfer begins.

bounded_authority.evidence: ISO 15118-20 Clause 10 (Smart Charging) defines charge schedules with power/current limits and time boundaries (ScheduleExchange). ISO 15118-20 Clause 11 (V2G) defines discharge authority windows. However, the standard does not define explicit 'agent revocation' or 'override by human' mechanisms for autonomous third-party agents; authority is bounded within the charging session scope only.
bounded_authority.rationale: Authority is bounded through schedule envelopes and power ceilings, but revocation, third-party delegation expiry, and human-override clauses are not explicitly addressed.

decision_auditability.evidence: ISO 15118-2 Clause 9 (Metering) and ISO 15118-20 Clause 13 define metered values and require signed meter reports (MeteringReceipt). However, no clause explicitly requires logging or attribution of agent-specific decisions beyond the EV-SECC pair; the meter receipt provides billing-grade data but not a decision log.
decision_auditability.rationale: Auditability is limited to metering receipts; there is no explicit requirement for logging agent decisions, attributing decisions to specific agents, or maintaining an audit trail of control actions.

data_governance.evidence: ISO 15118-20 Annex C references privacy considerations and TLS encryption (Clause 8) for securing communication. ISO 15118-2 Clause 7.2 requires secure communication channels but does not define data ownership, user consent mechanisms, or data retention policies.
data_governance.rationale: Transport-layer security is required, but ownership, explicit consent flows, and retention/erasure rules are not defined — these are deferred to contractual or regulatory frameworks.
